arxiv-2107-08113.title: Single-photon detection with a Josephson junction coupled to a resonator
arxiv-2107-08113.creator: Dmitry S. Golubev 1, Evgeni V. Il’ichev 2,3, Leonid S. Kuzmin 4,5
arxiv-2107-08113.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Dmitry S. Golubev 1, Evgeni V. Il’ichev 2,3, Leonid S. Kuzmin 4,5. We use semiclassical formalism to optimize a microwave single photon detector based on switching events of a current biased Josephson junction coupled to a resonator. In order to detect very rare events, the average time between dark counts τ dark \tau_{\rm dark} should be maximized taking into account that the switching time τ sw \tau_{\rm sw} should be sufficiently small.

arxiv-2203-04460.title: Model for independent particle motion
arxiv-2203-04460.creator: A. V. Afanasjev
arxiv-2203-04460.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by A. V. Afanasjev. Independent particle model in nuclear physics assumes that the nucleon in the nucleus moves in the average (mean field) potential generated by all other nucleons. This chapter gives a short overview of basic features of the independent particle motion in atomic nuclei and its theoretical realization in the framework of shell models for spherical, deformed and rotating nuclei as well as in more sophisticated approaches such as microscopic+macroscopic model and density functional theories.

arxiv-2403-03603.title: Large charge fluctuations in the Hierarchical Coulomb gas
arxiv-2403-03603.creator: Alon Nishry, Oren Yakir
arxiv-2403-03603.description: Abstract . The two-dimensional one-component plasma (OCP) is a model of electrically charged particles which are embedded in a uniform background of the opposite charge, and interact through a logarithmic potential. More than 30 years ago, Jancovici, Lebowitz and Manificat discovered an asymptotic law for probabilities of large charge fluctuations in the OCP.

arxiv-2406-01420.title: An absence of binary companions to Wolf-Rayet stars in the Small Magellanic Cloud Thanks: Based on observations collected at the European Organisation for Astronomical Research in the Southern Hemisphere under ESO programme 108.22M1.001.
arxiv-2406-01420.creator: A. Schootemeijer, T. Shenar, N. Langer, N. Grin, H. Sana, G. Gräfener, C. Schürmann, C. Wang, X.-T. Xu
arxiv-2406-01420.description: Abstract In order to predict the black hole mass distributions at high redshift, we need to understand whether very massive single stars ( M ∼ > 40 M\mathrel{\hbox{\hbox to0.0pt{\hbox{\lower 4.0pt\hbox{$\sim$}}\hss}\hbox{$>$}}}40 M ⊙ ) at low metallicity Z Z lose their hydrogen-rich envelopes, like their metal-rich counterparts, or whether a binary companion is required to achieve this.

arxiv-2505-15162.title: AI Solutionism and Digital Self-Tracking with Wearables CCS: Human-centered computing HCI theory, concepts and models
arxiv-2505-15162.creator: Hannah R. Nolasco, Andrew Vargo, Koichi Kise
arxiv-2505-15162.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Hannah R. Nolasco, Andrew Vargo, Koichi Kise. Self-tracking technologies and wearables automate the process of data collection and insight generation with the support of artificial intelligence systems, with many emerging studies exploring ways to evolve these features further through large-language models (LLMs). This is done with the intent to reduce capture burden and the cognitive stress of health-based decision making, but studies neglect to consider how automation has stymied the agency and independent reflection of users of self-tracking interventions.

arxiv-2507-02234.title: Gravitational Redshift for Rapidly Rotating Neutron Stars
arxiv-2507-02234.creator: Zsombor Jakab, Sharon M. Morsink
arxiv-2507-02234.description: Abstract The Oblate Schwarzschild (OS) approximation is a method often used to compute the flux of X-rays emitted from a rapidly rotating neutron star. In this approximation, the oblate shape of the rotating star is embedded in the Schwarzschild metric, which is used to compute the redshift of photon energies as they propagate from the star to the telescope.

britannica-1911-slogan.description: Article 'Slogan' from the 1911 Encyclopædia Britannica (Volume 25), the classic English-language general encyclopedia, now in the public domain. pmc-10517673.title: Hospital Readiness and Perceived Health Professional Challenges to Prevent Pandemics in Gedeo Zone, Ethiopia: A Mixed-Method Study
pmc-10517673.creator: Abebayehu Zemedkun, Getnet Melaku, Seid Shumye, Addisu Alemayehu Gube, Hailemariam Mulugeta
pmc-10517673.description: BackgroundPandemics pose serious threats to health, society, and economy worldwide. Ethiopia has been affected by the COVID-19 pandemic, which has caused millions of deaths and disrupted essential health services. The readiness of health systems and the challenges that health professionals face in delivering pandemic-related services are crucial for preventing and controlling pandemics.

pmc-11391078.title: Spatial correlation assessment of multiple earthquake intensity measures using physics-based simulated ground motions
pmc-11391078.creator: Mohammad R. Zolfaghari, Mahboubeh Forghani
pmc-11391078.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Predictive models for spatial correlation play an effective role in the assessment of seismic risk associated with distributed infrastructure and building portfolios. However, existing models often rely on simplified approaches, assuming isotropy and stationarity. This paper verifies these assumptions by presenting a comprehensive study using a database of 3D physics-based simulated broadband ground motions for Istanbul, generated by the SPEED software. The results reveal significant event-to-event variability and nonstationary and anisotropic characteristics of spatial correlation influenced by source, path, and site effects.

pmc-11642280.title: Sex Differences in Clinical Features in Gout: A Nationwide Retrospective Cohort Study
pmc-11642280.creator: Hyunsue Do, Kwanyoung Choe, Min Jung Kim, Kichul Shin, Ki Won Moon
pmc-11642280.description: Background: Patients with gout have several coexisting conditions that impact mortality. We analyzed the differences in clinical manifestations among Korean patients with gout and compared the causes of death based on sex using data from the Korean National Health Insurance Service-National Sample Cohort database. Methods: We included adults with gout receiving urate-lowering therapy (ULT) from 2002 until 2019.

pmc-12442146.title: Cefepime continuous infusion as a part of antibiotic stewardship against MDR: NICU of Cipto Mangunkusumo Hospital (CMH) experience
pmc-12442146.creator: Muhammad Azharry Rully, Putri Maharani Tristanita Marsubrin, Rosalina Dewi Roeslani, Ahmad Kautsar, Nina Dwi Putri, Jessica Sylvania Oswari
pmc-12442146.description: Background: As the incidences of preterm births and surgical cases increases, so do cases of neonatal sepsis in CMH. Furthermore, the common etiology of neonatal sepsis are multidrug-resistant bacteria which increase the risk of mortality. Cefepime is a fourth-generation cephalosporin which is increasingly being utilized in NICUs.

pmc-12587168.title: Exploring the mechanisms of mutual influence between lactylation and macrophage polarization in the context of disease
pmc-12587168.creator: Houhua Guo, Nannan Luan, Jian Gao, Xiaoao Pang, Jianlei Bi, Liancheng Zhu
pmc-12587168.description: BackgroundLactylation, a post‐translational alteration facilitated by lactic acidderived lactyl‐CoA, has emerged as an epigenetic regulator that alters gene expression in macrophages. Emerging data situates lactylation at the nexus of metabolic flux and immune cell destiny, especially in tumor and inflammatory microenvironments.

pmc-12678992.title: Clinical value of predicting bleeding after endoscopic submucosal dissection for early esophageal cancer
pmc-12678992.creator: Sheng-Nan Liu, Zhuo Chen
pmc-12678992.description: BACKGROUNDThe incidence of esophageal cancer is high, and its prognosis is poor. Endoscopic submucosal dissection (ESD) is an important, minimally invasive treatment for early esophageal cancer, but the risk of postoperative bleeding affects its efficacy.AIMTo explore risk factors of bleeding after ESD and evaluate the predictive value of a gradient boosting machine (GBM) model for postoperative bleeding.

pmc-13198136.title: Ventricular Fibrillation Without Hemodynamic Deterioration
pmc-13198136.creator: Jasmin Zernikow, Isabella Hintz, Sebastian Spethmann, Jan Gröschel, Nikolaos Dagres, Felix Schoenrath, Gerhard Hindricks, Christoph Knosalla, Friedrich Koehler, Wilhelm Haverkamp
pmc-13198136.description: BackgroundHeterotopic heart transplantation (HHT) is rarely performed in contemporary practice and poses distinct electrophysiological challenges due to the coexistence of the patient's native heart and the transplanted donor organ.Case summaryWe present the case of a 56-year-old man who experienced recurrent ventricular arrhythmias 6 years post-HHT.

pmc-13487236.title: Canine “Sniffin’ Sticks” enable behavioural olfactometry to complement neurological examination in dogs
pmc-13487236.creator: L H Hagemann, H A Volk, M Prielipp, N Power Guerra, A Sabiniewicz, T Hummel, S Meller
pmc-13487236.description: Olfactory function assessment in dogs remains limited compared to human medicine. This study aimed to develop a canine version of “Sniffin’ Sticks” (canSSt) as a clinical behavioural olfactometry tool and to establish normative olfactory thresholds across sex, age, and cranial morphology in dogs. Eighty healthy client-owned dogs underwent clinical and neurological examination.
